questions.question: Gautama Buddha decided to find his own path to realisation, and meditated for days on end under a tree at Bodh Gaya in Bihar.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Peepal.
  • Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (Nirvana) at the age of 35 under a Peepal tree (Bodhi Tree) in Bodh Gaya, Bihar.
  • He was born as Siddhartha Gautama in the Sakya clan.
  • Important Exam Fact: His first sermon was delivered at Sarnath, known as Dhammacakkappavattana.

questions.question: Which of the following Acts allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rowlatt Act.
  • Passed in 1919, this act gave the British government enormous powers to repress political activities.
  • It allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for up to two years.
  • Mahatma Gandhi called it the 'Black Act'.

questions.question: Ashoka’s dhamma __________ worship of a god, or performance of a sacrifice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is did not involve.
  • Ashoka's Dhamma was a set of edicts that formed a policy of social ethics.
  • It did not involve the worship of a god or performance of sacrifices.
  • It emphasized Ahimsa (non-violence) and respect for elders and monks.

questions.question: Who among the following social reformers founded the Self Respect Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Periyar.
  • E.V. Ramasamy, popularly known as Periyar, founded the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.
  • The movement aimed at achieving a society where backward castes have equal human rights.
  • It was a significant movement in Tamil Nadu against Brahminical dominance.

questions.question: In which year was the Rowlatt Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1919.
  • The Rowlatt Act was officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act.
  • It was passed by the Imperial Legislative Council in March 1919.
  • Protests against this act led to the tragic Jallianwala Bagh Massacre.

questions.question: Mauryan Empire in India was established in 322 B.C. with its capital in Pataliputra which is now known as __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Patna.
  • The Mauryan capital Pataliputra is the modern-day city of Patna in Bihar.
  • It was strategically located at the confluence of the Ganges, Ganda, and Son rivers.
  • It remained a power center for the Magadha, Maurya, and Gupta empires.

questions.question: The Dandi March, led by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, was a significant protest against which British policy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Salt tax.
  • The Dandi March (March-April 1930) was a direct action campaign against the British salt monopoly.
  • Gandhiji walked from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi to break the salt law.
  • This event inaugurated the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question: The last and ______ tirthankara of the Jainas was Vardhamana Mahavira.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 24th.
  • Vardhamana Mahavira was the 24th and last Tirthankara of Jainism.
  • The 23rd Tirthankara was Parshvanatha.
  • Mahavira added the concept of Brahmacharya (celibacy) to the existing four vows of Jainism.

questions.question: In which year, Alexander invaded India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 326 BC.
  • Alexander the Great invaded the Indian subcontinent in 326 BC.
  • He fought the famous Battle of the Hydaspes against King Porus.
  • His army refused to advance further east across the Beas River due to exhaustion and the fear of the Nanda Empire.

questions.question: Which ancient text, attributed to the sage Vyasa, is a central epic of ancient India and consists of 100,000 verses in 18 parvas (books)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mahabharata.
  • The Mahabharata is attributed to sage Vyasa and is one of the world's longest epics.
  • It contains about 100,000 verses divided into 18 Parvas (books).
  • The Bhagavad Gita is a part of the Bhishma Parva of this epic.

questions.question: Indian Muslims launched the Khilafat Movement under the leadership of ; popularly known as the Ali brothers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
  • The Khilafat Movement (1919-1924) was led by the Ali Brothers.
  • It was a protest against the humiliation of the Ottoman Caliph (Khalifa) after WWI.
  • Gandhiji supported it to foster Hindu-Muslim unity during the Non-Cooperation Movement.

questions.question: In which year was the Arms Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1878.
  • The Indian Arms Act was passed by Lord Lytton in 1878.
  • It prohibited Indians from carrying weapons without a license, but Europeans were exempted.
  • This discriminatory policy was a major grievance for Indian nationalists.

questions.question: During the ancient period in India, the term ‘sandhi-vigrahika’ was used to refer to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Minister of war and peace.
  • In ancient Indian administration (especially Gupta era), the Sandhi-vigrahika was a high-ranking official.
  • The term literally means Minister of War and Peace (Diplomacy).
  • The poet Harisena held this position under Samudragupta.

questions.question: Who established India's first girl's school?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Savitribai Phule.
  • Savitribai Phule along with her husband Jyotirao Phule established India's first girls' school in 1848 at Bhide Wada, Pune.
  • She is regarded as the mother of Indian feminism.
  • She worked extensively for the education of Dalits and women.

questions.question: The_______ repeals the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita Bill.
  • The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) was introduced to replace the British-era Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860.
  • It is part of a reform to decolonize the Indian legal system.
  • Important: It was passed along with Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Bill (BSB).

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Khudai Khidmatgars?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.
  • He founded the Khudai Khidmatgars ('Servants of God') in 1929.
  • He is popularly known as the Frontier Gandhi and his followers were called 'Red Shirts'.
  • He was a staunch believer in non-violence and the first non-Indian to receive the Bharat Ratna.

questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler was the grandson of Chandragupta Maurya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ashoka.
  • The Mauryan lineage was: Chandragupta Maurya (Grandfather) → Bindusara (Father) → Ashoka (Grandson).
  • Ashoka is famous for the Kalinga War (261 BC) and spreading Buddhism.
  • He was the first ruler to communicate with people through inscriptions.

questions.question: The Doctrine of Lapse was devised by Governor General __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Lord Dalhousie.
  • The Doctrine of Lapse was an annexation policy followed by Lord Dalhousie (1848–1856).
  • According to this, any princely state without a natural heir would be annexed by the British.
  • States like Satara, Sambalpur, and Jhansi were annexed under this policy.

questions.question: The Iron Age in India is associated with the ___________ period, which lasted from about 1500 to 500 BCE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Vedic.
  • The Iron Age in India (approx. 1500–500 BCE) coincides with the Vedic Period.
  • Iron tools helped in clearing dense forests of the Gangetic plains for agriculture.
  • The use of Painted Grey Ware (PGW) is also associated with this period.

questions.question: The Jallianwala Bagh Massacre took place in Amritsar in 1919, during which policy or act that allowed the British to arrest and imprison Indians without trial?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Rowlatt Act.
  • The massacre on April 13, 1919, occurred when people gathered to protest the Rowlatt Act and the arrest of leaders Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.
  • General Dyer ordered the firing in the enclosed Jallianwala Bagh.
  • This event led Rabindranath Tagore to renounce his Knighthood.

questions.question: The most common tool for the Iron Age was the __________, Which was used for felling trees, chopping wood, and as a weapon.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Axe.
  • The Axe was a primary iron tool used for clearing forests during the later Vedic period/Iron Age.
  • It enabled the expansion of agriculture into the fertile plains.
  • Iron technology also led to the development of better ploughshares.

questions.question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati was the founder of which of the following reform association?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.
  • Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 in Bombay.
  • He gave the slogan 'Go back to the Vedas'.
  • He authored the famous book Satyarth Prakash.

questions.question: Which of the following Indian cities is associated with the Sangam literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Madurai.
  • Madurai was the capital of the Pandyas and the center of Sangam Literature assemblies.
  • Sangam literature is the earliest known literature of South India (Tamil).
  • Three Sangams (academies of poets) were held under the patronage of Pandya kings.

questions.question: Who was the social reformer and political leader who championed women's rights and played a significant role in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar.
  • He was a key figure in the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.
  • He served as the principal of Sanskrit College, Kolkata.
  • He was given the title 'Vidyasagar' (Ocean of Knowledge) for his vast learning.

questions.question: The ___________ Empire was established in 322/321 B.C. by the great king Chandragupta.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Mauryan.
  • The Mauryan Empire was founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 322 BC after defeating the Nanda dynasty.
  • He was assisted by his mentor and strategist, Chanakya (Kautilya).
  • It was the first major pan-Indian empire.
